This drug should be off the market and the makers of it need to go back to the laboratory and further perfect it.

For the past year I had been taking Orsythia which was switched to Aviane two months ago. No complaints. Actually I've never had any trouble with birth control pills ever. Last weekend I went in to pick up my refill which was another generic of the same brand called...Falmina. I can't even stand hearing that name now. Within a few days of taking it I felt insanely bloated stomach pains extreme chest pains and cramping that still won't go away even though I stopped taking it....I had to call another pharmacy to find Aviane and return this one. Do not take this medicine!!! It will most likely make you quite ill!!!

I started this medication after my pharmacy substituted this for Aviane. Since day one of starting i have experienced severe migraine headaches, dark urine, and chest pain/pressure. After one week i have to decided to go back to Aviane and just pay extra at another pharmacy. Falmina was the WORST!!! I"ve felt sick to to stomach and very Nauseous. DO NOT TAKE!! You"ve been warned..

I have been on Aviane for 3 months now. I don't always take it at the same time, but close to the time I normally take it. I have never missed a day taking the pill. When I first started it I felt a bit woozy and I did have spotting. Now everything is fine and normal- no pregnancy yet. Do not have sex unless you are married. Never EVER have unprotected sex! unprotected sex=STD, which is worse than pregnancy at a young age. Some STD's will remain with you for life, and some can kill you!

Had to switch to this from Levora that worked great. Even though Portia kept me from getting pregnant, I woke up every morning with cramps, nausea and by week 3 I had purpura show up on my legs. I had back pain and mood swings like crazy.

Portia was the first birth control I was put on and I have been on Portia now for 6 years. I wanted a birth control that would not cause weight gain, and I don't believe it has. I went through a stint of mid acne 3 years in and has cleared up since I changed my skin care routine. I used to have 7 day moderate-heavy periods and now have it for 1 day with 1-2 days of spotting after. Within the past year when I have been stressed for exams or with life in general, I haven't gotten my period which may be due to the extreme lightness in the first place. The only real problem is I forget to take them at the exact same time every day, or have forgotten to take them a few days in a row. Even so, I have had no pregnancies.

I began Levora about 10 months ago to help ease my endometriosis. It did minimize the pain to only the first couple days of my period, but the side effects were horrible. I became extremely depressed--anxious, nauseous, moody, crying constantly. It killed my entire sex drive, almost ruining my relationship. My social life also crumbled. I have been off Levora for the past month and feel amazing. This pill ruined my life! I almost would have rather had the endometriosis pain. And saying that means a lot.

ok 1st mth no bleed 2nd mth spotted all mth light bleed 3rd mth after shot if been spotting bleeding all mth....uggg 


i got it for prevent period and heavy bleeding...omg ive been bleeding forever... i will not get my 2nd shot... thank goodness i didnt gain weight...
Is it normal to not get a period for months after.  I only took it once for endrometriosis... It didn't help.  I got the shot in August and haven't had one since and no period.

The treatment has been great. After having 3 kids I needed a temporary contraception until my husbands vasectomy was done. I have been on this shot for 6 months and have not had a period, which is fine by me.I have had mood swings which is normal. If you are gaining more then 20pds on the shot it is you not the shot. If you read up on it you do gain a little weight, but not 100 pounds. I did gain 10, but also I have 3 kids and not have been eating the way I should. I have only one more time to take the shot and then will be done, but I think it has been a great alternative to the pill which I had tried 10 different kinds and they all made me sick and the nuvo ring is how I got pregnant with my 1st child.

I started taking this medication because birth control pills make me ill. I have been on it for 7 or more years (I can't really remember). I have no problems expect for weight gain and it messing with my blood sugar numbers. In November 2013, I had breakthrough bleeding that lasted 2 1/2 months. I even went in to see my NP for my yearly and shot which didn't help anything--still bled. She suggested I go see her MD. Right before my appt I stopped bleeding. She suggested a uterine ablation because the Depo may not help me anymore. I just had that done and am due for my next shot which I am not getting. I have PCOS--this is why I have always had horendous periods. We will see if I still need to be on this in a couple of months. I was pleased with the Depo shot but am going to look forward to not having to get poked every 3 months. This drug was a Godsend for me. It may not be for you. By the way I am 47 and have no intention of having any more kids.

Haven't gotten pregnant so far, which is a plus. I've been on it for a year now after finding out that depo provera causes bone loss. The problem I have with this bc is that I get yeast infections on the regular and my period is always out of wack. Pills are always an inconvience. I'm still looking for something better.

I have only been on Beyaz for 4 days.  I am more agitated than ever and very easily angered over the simpliest things.  Then I find myself crying uncontrollably and feel like I am having a nervous breakdown.  I will be calling my doctor Monday to see if there is something else I can take.  I was on the depo shot for 2 years, had no periods or cramps or mood swings but gained 20lbs and then starting getting really really fatiged.  Dr. told me I was just depressed and then it got worse so I went to another dr. who tested my horomone levels.  The shot was making me go through EARLY MENOPAUSE at 30 yrs old!!!  I hope I find something that works for me soon, the whole reason I'm need b-controle is to controle my irregular and painful periods.

After trying 4  different BC pills post surgical laparoscopy for endometriosis ( stage 4) and multiple ovarian masses I finally found Natazia. I spotted for months ( every stinkin day plus a breakthrough week of bleeding even while on active pills) with Junel, then generess fe I put on 7 lbs in 1 month, plus spotting. I was ready to give it up and just let the masses grow back and the endo rage on and as a last ditch effort we tried Natizia. I've been on it for two months no without a period without a single day of spotting. Lost all the weight, limited bloating and light mood swings. I feel so normal! Thank you Natazia!!

I have been using birth control pills since 2004. Most recently, I was on Yaz, but had terrible mood swings, depression, and a loss of libido.  I love Natazia.  I feel normal... my mood is stable and my libido is fine. I did have some break-through bleeding during my first three packs, but that has subsided. My only complaint is the price of $80 (with insurance)! That's ridiculous.

I've been pleased with the effectiveness as far as not becoming pregnant, something that wasn't the case with my previous BC.
However, I'm glad my last Natazia pill was yesterday because it's been 18 months of awful.  I've experienced severe weight gain, numbness in my legs, sleep problems, extreme mood swings, increased PMS symptoms, horrid cramping, and irregular periods (although there was a span of about 7 months where it was very regular), none of which would be the norm in my 18 years of menstruation.
And it's only been recently that I finally figured out that all of these issues were linked to the same thing and had started not long after starting on this pill.

topics.top_condition: Premenstrual Disorder with a State of Unhappiness
example_quotes: Rated it a 5 in effectiveness as it did do what it's intended to do but started the pill in February and the past 1-2 months have been miserable for me. Incredibly depressed and anxious, mood swings like I've never expierenced them before, crying randomly, not wanting to see my boyfriend or close friends, loss of interest in a ton of things. Decreased sex drive, not wanting anything to do with intimacy, hot flashes, my boobs have gotten bigger & are very tender.. I'm convinced it's either this pill or PMDD.
Extreme problems with PMDD were cured within the first month of usage. Few side effects besides initial spotting. Also helps with acne.
This drug has been a great help for me.  However, my pharmacist has told me that they have discontinued it. Does anyone know why or of anything else that works as well as Sarafem?

topics.top_condition: Bipolar I Disorder with Most Recent Episode Mixed
example_quotes: Have taken everything from Wellbutrin to Depakote to Tegretol and many others, nothing worked. Kind of leary when Dr. prescribed this sublingual, but the difference is amazing! I HATE the taste and when it dissolves it fills my mouth with saliva as well as numbs my tongue.  I also hate having to wait ten minutes after to eat or drink. It's the worst part of my day.  However, prior to starting this medicine I was constantly thinking about suicide or attempting it, my moods were all over the place with rage, impatience, and lack of motivation and I hadn't written anything worthwhile in over a year.  I also was only getting about two hours of sleep a night.  This medication does make me drowsy so, I take it right before I go to bed and sleep like a baby, waking up pert and perky (something that's never happened until now).  No signs of depression or suicidal thoughts and I love the fact that I feel like a normal woman.  It's really been a miracle for me and even my husband has noticed. I've been on this about a week, so I hope Saphris is the one for me. So far I haven't had any negative side effects.

I had to stop using saphris due to it started eating away at the skin of my lower front gums. Was very disappointed, because the medication was helping. The first med in a long time that helped without weight gain.

I started Saphris after unsuccessful on seroquel, zyprexa, abilify, risperdal. Results are great for me so far. Benefits include no more suspicious odors of harmful impact. Side effects are very low.  My motivation level is through the roof, it is not really restlessness and it is not really akathisia. I don't have anxiety any more like I did on the other meds. I have to take trazadoone for sleep since saphris interferes with my sleep.

I have been diagnosed with Parkinson 4 months ago. I am taking 1 mg Azilect and 4 mg Requip.  My wife tells me that I have less tremors when I sleep. Side symptoms are bad. I am lethargic and sleepy all the time, have nausea, and vivid dreams that interfere with my sleep. I am not sure if these drugs improves my shakiness and stiffness symptoms. Also, I am not sure if the side effects are caused by the Azilect, the Requip or both.

I'm one of the children in the traumatic brain injury study...14 years later.  At 31, I still take amantadine and it still works. With this medication, I was able to graduate high school and a university, and keep a full time job.  I'm also a writer, and amantadine helps me perform better-than-average there, as well. It controls tremors in my hands and my ability to think clearly.

I haven't seen (m)any side effects in the decade, plus, I've been on it; however, when it is time for another dose or I'm all out for the day, my thoughts become muddled and speech slightly slurred...No super-late night driving (without extra dose(s)!

I took Amantidine in a double blind study to see the effectiveness of this drug on patients with head injury causing cognitive impairment following brain injury. Was pleased with this medicine and the results I recieved from it.

The first few days weren't bad but then I started getting confused and it was hard to concentrate.  Then my blood pressure skyrocketed and I started having severe twitching and muscle jerking.  It was terrible.  I was on it for a week but the side effects were too severe so my dr took me off of it.  Tried another drug but not having much luck with it either.  Still searching for a drug that works for me...
I have still had some difficulty with a twitching leg in the evening, but recently was put on a stronger dose.  The twitching is better, but I am fatigued and want to try a smaller dose.
After several years of trying to get BS Spikes under control, my Dr recently prescribed Invokana and after only 4 days,the spikes are gone.
MY  THINKING  TWITCH  ONCE  EVERYDAY  AND  I  MOVED  VERY  SLOWLY.
Great med-only issue is I have developed twitching of my facial muscles...I don'/t notice it others do.
Noticed small, jerky involuntary movements of legs, arms and abdominal muscles
causes shaky hands, sometimes so much so that it can impair my ability of fine motor skills
Only have been on the drug for a couple of days. My nerologist put me on the drug because I have involuntary tremors of hands and they also shake at different times throughtout the day.
GAD plus parkinson like tremors made getting to sleep difficult but after a year Iconstantly get up early(4am)

Medication worked well for three months. Then night sweats and heat flashes returned just as frequently as they did prior to its usage. I stopped taking brisdelle after 5 months and had trouble with withdraw symptoms. I had what seemed to feel like brain zaps off and on for about a month after I stopped using it! Hope it works better for other ladies!

Update- after a few months on this medication I stopped taking it, so far so good as the hot flashes and night sweats have not returned. I stopped taking Brisdelle because I couldn't stand the weight gain, headaches, and I hated that it killed my libido.  There ARE side effects.  If I have to start it again, I will b/c it does offer some relief. But for me- after a while the side effects weren't worth it. I hope I can stay off this medication. For what it's worth- I rarely take prescription medication unless there is simply no other option. I'd rather try herbs again than go on Brisdelle.

I went to see my Dr. Just so she could prescribe this.   I have been having hot flashes for 10 years now.  The last few years they have been pretty severe and frequent and I wasn't able to get a good night's sleep without waking about every hour to hour and a half with horrible sweats and discomfort. By the end of the work week I would end up with headaches and feeling worn out.  I was hoping that this drug would save me from all of that.   Well, not quite but it has helped.  
Also, it is very expensive at about $150.00 a month and my insurance would not cover it because it was a new off label drug, and some other red tape BS.  From what I understand Brisdelle is a 7.5mg dose of Paxil or the generic drug Paroxitine. The lowest dose of Paroxitine available is 10mg. So, I asked my Dr. to prescribe that instead. It costs me $4 per month.  
Now as to how it works for me.   I take it at bedtime.  At first it did seem to work pretty well but now on my third month it's not doing so much.  During the day I still have flashes but most of them seem not as intense or long lasting.  The nights I do sleep better and when I do wake up hot, it's not as bad or long lasting as before.  So it had helped some.  I guess I was really hoping for a cure for the insane discomfort of having these shit - storm hot flashes!   Ugh.  Will they never end?!
Now, in talking with my Dr.she did tell me she can up the dosage if the minimum doesn't work.  I'm going to try that next.  If that doesn't work I suppose I'll just continue to suffer until someone figures out what causes this Hell.
For me I haven't noticed any side effects.

I went in yesterday for insertion. I read up on all these reviews talking about how awful the pain was and all of the cramping that takes place after-it got me so worried. Especially since it's supposed to be worse for women who haven't had children.
My experience wasn't bad at all. The pain during insertion is pretty bad, I won't lie, but it's definitely bearable. It's a really sharp pain and then some bad cramping but it goes away relatively quickly. I had some mild cramping shortly after but I took a nap and they've been gone ever since.
Don't let the other reviews freak you out, it really isn't so bad.
Love it. Just had my second one inserted a week ago. Had cramping for a few hours and no spotting at all. wish is wasnt so expensive though. R2 200 South African Rands.

From the beginning 3 years ago, I have had bad pelvic cramps, depression, swollen stomach, large weight gain, hives and joint pain.  Planning to have the device removed as soon as my insurance takes effect.

I've been taking Ocella for 5 years...It was originally prescribed to help with my acne which it has been more than successful in that area. I take 4 packs continuously (skipping the placebos, jumping straight to the active) for 84 days and then I have a cycle...my cycle only lasts 3-4 days which is amazing considering I only have 4 cycles a year on this medication...Only side effect is the blurred vision that occurs from time to time lasting 10-30 minutes. Other than that I am very satisfied with this product and I've never had a pregnancy scare. :)

I switched from Yasmine to Ocella a month ago, as the pharmacy asked me if it would bother me to take a generic.  I broke out in terrible hives; with welts from my eyes to my ankles.  I segregated by morning pills and found it was Ocella causing the allergic reaction.  I called the pharmacist and the gynecologist, and they both stated it was unusual as Yasmine and Ocella have the same active ingredients.  Judging by the comments contained here, I would say it is not uncommon.  I was able to remedy it by taking benedryl on my own to counter the allergic reaction...I started back on Yasmine, and everything seems to be o.k.

I switched to Ocella from another birth control to help with PMDD. I had suffered very depressed moods and crying one week before and during my period. I started taking Ocella about a month ago and I already see a difference in my moods. I have not felt nearly as horrible as I did before. The first week or so taking ocella, I had stomach aches every night, but that's typical when switching to any new medicine. I am satified so far, and hope it continues. It is my 3rd day on the reminder pills and I have yet to start my period, so we'll see what happens! Very happy with it.
I go for lab work, they check my count and determine if I need injection. Some months I do and other months I do not need injection.
I have an injection once a month by my doctor for carcinoid cancer. Five months without any problems.
painful injection site with eventual local tissue swelling up to 6cm after.Injector i found was not always easy to use.I had a number of med not being injected

I have been taking Mononessa for three months and still have terrible breast tenderness. My breasts are so tender it hurts to touch and sometime even my bra makes them hurt. Not only that but around the beginning of the third pack my emotions went crazy. I cry for almost no reason at all and get really angry quickly which I have never had a problem with.

I have been taking mononessa for 4 years and decided to stop. I am very concerned tbh. I have some of the worst luck ever and with my family jinxing me every 5 mins, I prolly should've gotten pregnant by now. I know some BC can make you infertal after a long time, I'm worried that's what happened to me....

I got on this birth control 8 weeks post partum after having my son in October, been on it for one month, i liked it. took away my lochia bleeding and also had no side effects. didn't have insurance for awhile then got on Sprintec because it didn't cost much, didn't like that had a lot of side effects. so i switched back to Mononessa because i liked the results i was having from it when i first took it. i started having nausea, sometimes vomiting, cramps spotting a week before period and still spotting now when i started my water pills. and i  back acne, never had it in my life.

topics.top_condition: Multiple Sclerosis Symptoms Return then Become Less Severe
example_quotes: Mild flushing on first dose, and more on first 240 dose. Just rode out the heat, like a sunburn or pepper spray, last 20 minutes. No other issues, food just delays the reaction, take it right before you eat, especially fats. No other meds taken, just vitamins, and probiotics, no beef, no sugar, no sat fat.

I can't give this a proper review I guess, as I only took 1 tablet of the lower dose. I had such an awful flushing, skin crawling rash I did some research on the internet. I decided to stop taking it as I found out it was designed to be sprayed on leather furniture to stop it going moldy in storage. It was then banned as it caused people to get rashes when sitting on sofas. After that I didn't fancy eating it TBH!!!

First dose and I had a long flushing episode.  It was painful and my face was swollen and I thought I was experiencing an allergic reaction as I am allergic to many meds.  Saw MD to confirm it was not.  Little stomach upset but I am on prescription GERD meds.  I waited for the release of this drug and I want to maintain optimism that this oral will work.  For those with flushing--how long were the episodes?

I have been taking Beyaz for almost 7 months now and feel that it is doing exactly what it is supposed. I am not pregnant. As for mood swings and other side effects, yes there are some. I noticed when I first started taking it they were considerably worse, mostly the mood swings and feeling emotional. After sticking it out and not switching after 2 months like most people decide to do I am very pleased with it. I would recommend this BC to pill, I was on orthro tri cyclen lo before it and hated that!

I was prescribed Beyaz for PMDD and help with my period. The first two months were normal, with my normal PMDD symptoms. By my third month my period had become heavy and lasted for three weeks. After my three week period ended I continued to have irregular bleeding & spot up until the fifth month. I didn't care about the PMDD so much because I was listless and tired all the time. After calling my doctor I was given an ultrasound and had bloodwork done. This had rendered me anemic. I'll never take Beyaz again. I've been on birth control for over 5 years and never had the problems this gave me.

I'm actually not sure if I'm somewhat satisfied with byaz but I can say it has helped my PMDD symptoms.  Previously I was not on any bc and I had SEVERE cramps and mood swings.  Now I barely have any cramps and I haven't noticed any mood swings.  My appetite has also decreased slightly.  The possible problem: I now have a weird rash that comes and goes on my face that my dermatologist has labeled as "a strange eczema".  The rash developed after I started the medication but my Derm doesn't think it's from the byaz. . .

Agreed to try vaccine for a trial study, but pain is horrible. Can't sleep, can barely dress myself, if anything touches my arm even lightly, the pain is unbearable.  I'm also hot, nauseous, and have back/head pain. (day 2)

Receiving this injection was somewhat painful for the first and second shots, however the third was extremely painful and caused more problems where therapy and movement and never recovered to pre-injection status.

The first time I got the shot it was as they say, mild bone pain. The second and third time were soooo awful. After 24 hrs my bones, muscles, skin, you name it hurt head to toe. I could not be touched. It was all I could do to roll over in bed. I felt like I'd been hit by a truck. I understand an infection can be deadly and that the two days of debilitating pain were better than death. But I definately had to be talked into that last dose by my doctor, and if it came down to me getting that shot again or coming down with cholora, berry-berry some deadly infection or whatever I would probably take my chances. A body can take just so much.

I had surgery for my right knee 5 months ago. I had  two tears in the meniscus, stage 4 arthritis, and inflamation of the synovial membrane. My recovery was slow so my Doctor recommended the euflexxia. I wanted into the office for my first injection. The shot was extremely painful. When I went for my second injection, I walked in on one crutch. Two days later, I was on both crutches and unable to do any weight bearing on my knee. I opted not to carry through with the third injection. Today 3 1/2 weeks later I am still on two crutches. The nauseating bone ache is finally gone, and I can put weight on my knee, but I am back to where I started after surgery and will have to start at square one with therapy. I would give anything to go back where I was before the injections.

I took this medication for eight years after having an accident and othroscopic surgery on right knee.  The last two years, I found it became less and less effective.  Finally saw a surgeon and had knee replacement.  The euflexxia hots bought me some years before major surgery, I was bone on bone and knew eventually it had go be done.

My doctor is excellent, Dr. Blobeck, [NAME_REDACTED], DTC in Denver, CO.

The application is critical to the success with three injections.  I have gone over a year between injections.  Would like to see mor flexibility, however, with no cartilidge remaining, 1000 times better than a knee replacement.  The gnarly verticle scar with lack of flexsion from replacement patients I've encountered will keep me on UFLEXXA as long as possible until cartilidge can be regrown with a medical breakthrough.

topics.top_condition: Chronic Inflammatory Skin Disease Marked by Blisters
example_quotes: I have been diagnosed with Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis after years of suffering. The dapsone works, however, stress really plays a part in my outbreaks and their severity. I HATE the blister packs!

I have been using Dapsone 100 mg/day for vitiligo treatment for 4 year. My patches were recovered quite effectively. There are no side-effects, except a rather pale skin which might caused by the drug. In brief, I feel satisfactory, hopeful but still anxious.

Diagnosed with Dermatitis Herpetiformis in about 1968. Initial dose 200mg per day .  Very effective at clearing skin blisters but severe headaches associated with the medication.  Went on gluten free diet in about 1970.  Reduced dosage to nil over 8 years.  Now have to take Dapsone occasionally even though very strict with diet.  Presumably more sensitive to gluten than I once was and some cross contamination in some manufactured foods that should be gluten free.  Does everyone now know that everyone with dH should be gluten free even if no gut symptoms?

I had success with the series of 3 shots, but the co-pays were becoming excessive. (Last series of 3 shots cost almost $600.) Decided to try Synvisc-One. Woke up in pain the first night. Ice & Aleve did not significantly help. Second night, more pain. Day 3 I am SO much pain it reminds me of when I had a burst Baker's cyst. I can hardly walk. Cannot straighten my knee nor bend it significantly.

I had Orthovisc injections (3) 7 months ago and it's still easing my knee pain.  I was told 3 years ago that I needed a new knee and now I can walk on my treadmill up to 20 minutes a day! The injections are no more painful than a cortisone injection.

20 -year-old water skiing injury tore mesicus cartilage, more acute pain in past two months.  Received 3 Orthovisc injections, not much relief.  Am following up with icing 8 hrs per day, cortisone shot today.  Cannot take NSAIDs.  Being told knee replacement when the pain becomes unbearable.  I'd like to hold that off as long as possible.  i week since last orthovisc, Dr. says I can begin swimming again on Monday.  Hoping to build femoral muscles to help relieve pain.  Taking Vicodin on weekends.

My knees were both very sore before the injections of Synvisc-one. The injections themselves were excruciating.And since the injections the pain is worse than before I had the injections. My knees are very stiff and feel unstable.At times I can't stand the pain and can barely walk for any length of time.I regret getting this done as I am much worse off than before and I didn't think that was possible.
Have had 3 synvisc-one shots with several cortizone also.  The first shot was good for seven months, second - maybe four, then cortizone --no good.  Third is the present one.

This is the 5th time I have had the one shot of Synvisc in each knee. I have moderate arthritis on the left and more severe on the right.  Most of my pain is right behind the knee caps - clicking, instability, pain, etc.  Getting the shots, I have had doctors use cooling spray to numb before and doctors who haven't.  To be honest, it doesn't make much difference.  The injection pain I experience on the left knee is tolerable.  The injection pain on the right knee is worse than getting a tooth drilled during childbirth.  That being said, I can tolerate it for the time it take to complete the injection (barely).  Afterwards, it takes me about 10 minutes before I can stand and it is generally painful for 24-48 hours.  Ice, ibupropen and rest.  The pressure is what hurts the most in my knees.  Both feel like balloon about to burst.  24 hours later, a little sore but much more stable and they feel stronger. 48 hours later, left feels about 98% healed, right knee is about 70%. After 5-7 days, it is all good.  For the 6-9 months of relieve I get from the shots, it is well worth it for me.

I am a 26 year old female, jRA since 4 yrs old. I rcved my 2nd shot today. The first one was pretty bad, the shot itself hurt and my knees had hurt in general  fairly badly. Today was my2nd shot and it was much better. They hurt right now, but not nearly as badly, but it's a different kind of pain.. hard to describe. The backs of my legs are tender as well. I seem to be moving a bit more freely. I am sincerely hoping this is a good sign.

Ever since I had the injections, I’ve had severe pain off and on, sometimes for hours.  My knee is now always tender where my tendons and ligaments fasten.  Before the shots, I had a pinch that would happen on the inside of my knee as I took each step.  After the first shot swelling of the lower leg started.  Within a few days of the second shot, my whole knee was sore.  After the third shot, I started losing bending range in my knee.  After two months, I still had severe pain.  An MRI was performed and it exposed a torn meniscus right where I was suffering the pinching sensation on the inside of my knee.  That has since been repaired, and the pinch has subsided, but all the other pain is still haunting me.  It has been four months since the shots and six weeks since the surgery.  I have yet to gain back my flexibility and I have the same pain that started after the shots and before the surgery.  The doctor continues to say, "give it time."

My doctor is awesome; I was in and out of his office in less than 5 minutes; shot was like a mosquito bite.  I was told it could take up to a month to get results.  Within two days my knee was no longer locking upon getting out of a chair.  The Synvisc One shot has been wonderful for me.  I had my first shot in April, 2011 and am getting another one tomorrow, December, 2011.

I had a great deal of pain in my knees for approximately 2 weeks after I had my IV.  After that, my knees started feeling better. In a few months, I could walk up our steps like I could when I was in my fifties (I am 74 years old).  It's been 15 months since I had my IV and my left knee is becoming painful and going out 0n me.  I am scheduled for another IV next week and I hope to get better.  I just hope that I do not have as much pain as I did the last time.

Had the third injection in both knees last Thursday.  First two went well, mild swelling, little pain.  Two days after the last injections I have a lot of swelling in both knees.  Rest, elevation and ice are not helping.  I have also been having severe lower leg cramps and found out I am anemic. I am hoping the swelling will go down.  I cannot exercise.  I can't walk or stand for very long.  I WILL NOT do this again.

My experience is conflicting.  Few minutes after I got the injection I went into a severe anaphylactic shock and ended in the ICU. After 12 hours I recovered and I am doing well but was a very horrible experience.  As for my knee I am satisfied with the product no pain at all and doing perfect. Obviously my body reacted in an abnormal way to this product.  After this experience I have to say that the product is not completely safe for everybody.   More investigation need to be done before the first death show up.

I was originally prescribed Balziva to treat my excessively painful periods. So far, so good. I experience little to no cramping now during my periods. However, I have had other side effects others have already mentioned: bleeding in between periods, breast tenderness, some nausea...I can live with the bleeding and the tenderness, and the nausea is only mildly irritating. This is the first birth control medicine I have ever been put on, and I think it works fine, if you're willing to put up with the side effects. Most people aren't going to be, though.

I am on this med for hormone inbalance. I was on FEMCON with great results (3 packs from the DR) and was given a rx for OVCON 35..my pharmacy gave me Balziva. OMG!! I've been on this for 9 days and I am ready to kill someone. No joke. I feel like I am in the middle of the worst PMS of my life. My breasts are tender, my moods are horrible. :( Called the pharmacy and they are sending out the brand name OVCON asap..it's going to cost me $30 a month, but my sanity and that of my family is worth every penny.

I suggest you think long and hard about taking this med..I know everyone is different, but this did not work for me. I read the reviews and was sure I wasn't going to have any issues....well, here I am on day 9 and I'm ready to blow my top..for no reason..at all. My kids and dh noticed a difference right away and asked if I was PMSing..I'm not..my period is 10 days away.

I recently switched from Aviane to Balziva. It has been kinda horrible. I've gained weight, felt slight nausea, stomach bloating and cramps and moodiness. Maybe it's because my body has not adjusted to it yet since I've only been on it for about 2 weeks.
Before sronyx I was taking ortho-evra in which I disliked a lot !!! I am very comfortable with this prescription.

Hello all! I have been taking Sronyx for about a month now and I absolutely love it. I switched over from Orthocept which was making me gain weight, have terrible cravings and wasn't helping my skin (something I think birth control should do). I also was very unstable emotionally but I don't fully blame Orthocept. I was really nervous after reading all the reviews on this site for Sronyx. I hadn't started taking it yet and so immediately I thought I was in for the worst. I got so worked up and it really was all for nothing. Sronyx has made my skin better, along with stabilizing my mood, increasing my sex drive and I've even lost a few pounds. I didn't have any side effects except for some mood swings but that's expected. Overall, I love Sronyx! P.S Reading reviews for birth control can be helpful to a point but our bodies/minds are all so different there is really no telling how birth control will effect you until you try it yourself :]

I used Sronyx for 3 months, I was hoping it would help decrease acne along with the birth control. The first month I was tired for 2 weeks and emotional.  My period was lighter but lasted 7 days instead of the normal 5.  The second month I noticed I broke out more while taking it, I wanted to try it out for 3 months before I considered changing brands.  By the third month, my acne was worse, period lasted longer and I lost about 14lbs(not a good thing).  I didn't realize I lost a significant amount of weight until I saw the doctor (to change my prescription). I am assuming my appetite had decreased. Oddly enough, I suffered weight loss rather than the latter.

I have been on Skyla for 8 months. I love it! Inserting it hurt and I felt like I was having a bad period the first two days. Minor spotting first few weeks. Minor 2-4 day periods first 3 months. No periods since! I lost weight from birth control pill and sex drive has increased. I sincerely recommend Skyla

I am jealous of you ladies who say getting the Skyla inserted wasn't painful for you! I had mine inserted 12 hours ago and I am STILL having extremely bad cramping and pain. My doctor gave me a prescription to soften my cervix, but even with the medicine it did not want to go in smoothly. My doctor actually had to squeeze my cervix to allow it to go in. Two big pops later and it was done, but man was it painful. And I have a pretty high pain tolerance. I had to stay at the office until my blood pressure came up, and they gave me some prescription strength ibuprofen but I still have some pain. Overall though, the 3 years of protection will be worth it.

I have been on the skyla for 4 months now, and I have sporadic cramps that come and go as they please. They are horrible. The skyla works great! But I can't handle the pain. Cramps come often after intercourse and with the cramps come bright red blood. Hoping this goes away with time. Got it checked out, Dr. said everything looks good under the hood.
I was recently switched from a different birth control to this one Falmina and I do not like it. I had no problem with my previous one, but this one gives me the worst acne.

I'm a non smoker, 5ft5 115lbs, exercise rarely (but active often), usual period before Aubra: mild to very uncomfortable cramps; heavy bleeding 2nd day, lasts 5-6 days

I've been taking the Aubra pill for two months now and haven't had any issues. My period lasted my usual 5 days, though it wasn't as heavy as usual. Cramps were significantly less painful & I've been happy with it so far! Plus I'm not pregnant - yippee !

I started on Aubra about a year ago when it was given to me at Planned Parenthood and recently have been experiencing a lot of spotting. It's not heavy bleeding but more of a dark consistency for about 3 weeks straight. I haven't had any other side effects as far as headaches or cramps though. After reading the other reviews it seems this isn't a rare thing. I guess I'll be going back to them to see about getting a different pill.
feel weird, sweating, insomnia
feeling cold and  night  sweats
I am sweating like no tomorrow

I have been taking this medicine for almost a year and it has really helps.I have been living with my MG for about four years and my sympton are double vision, slurred speech,diffculties swallowing and breathing.When I take my meds on time the meds work great!!!

Prescribed by neurologist for possible myasthenia gravis. Tests by an electrodiagnostic consultant indicated not myathenia gravis. Told to stop taking med. On it a total of three months. Am a blood donar, gallons up until now. They banned me from doing so because of the pyridostigmine bromide.

I was recently daignosed with Myasthenia Gravis. This drug, along with the time-release, is helping me be kept out of the ICU. I suffered a Myasthenic Crisis and I'm thankful that there is a drug out there that can prevent another crisis from happening. My teenage life wouldn't be the same without it. I take 3 60mg pills througout the day and one time-release at night, so in the morning I won't be as weak.

Taking Jolessa with the intent to minimize severe period discomfort and a heavy monthly flow, so that during menstruation I can have minimal distractions, ie stay at work, think, etc.

First pack: 25 days straight bleeding, day 21,22, bleeding through super tampons and pads. Day 24, bleeding out blood clots, cramping like food poisoning, extreme bloating. Discharge like a horror film. Very noticeable weight gain, probably 15lbs on the first 8 weeks of the pack. Taking a 5'-10" frame from 130 to 145, and not a frame that ever puts on weight, so it's quite abnormal. In addition, it definitely effects your mood, I'd say anger being the most present emotion, like all the time! I hate you Jolessa makers, how dare you think this is an acceptable drug for women.

I have only taken Jolessa for 8 days, as of today, after taking Seasonique for 5+ years satisfactorily. My only complaint about Seasonique was the cost even with insurance and with the new health care act that fully covers certain birth control now, I was simply looking for a less expensive, yet just as effective option. ($0 versus $150/3mos. is quite a difference!) However, I seem to be having some side effects (nausea, worsening & daily headaches, sleep disruption) that I'm not sure are related to the change to Jolessa or if I'm still recovering from whatever bug I had a couple of weeks ago. I also feel like I have a lump in my throat (a full feeling). The nausea makes it hard to determine whether I'm hungry or just nauseous. Since I am prone to migraines and had recently had my period, on top of a 100.2 degree fever for a couple of days, that included body aches and nausea and having to take a lot of Advil, I'm unsure whether I'm having rebound headaches and nausea caused from the Advil, or if it's actually the Jolessa. I will call my doctor, of course, if the symptoms do not go away soon (not sure how long to give it?) It would definitely be more cost effective to keep taking it, but I feel pretty miserable and might have to go back to Seasonique, which gave me no problems aside from having my period at unexpected times, which was minor compared to how I am feeling on a daily basis. I would be interested to know if anyone else has experienced the nausea, worsening headaches, etc. when switching from Seasonique to Jolessa or when beginning Jolessa, in general. I tend to be very sensitive to medication as it is, and I'm pretty good at trusting my gut, but any feedback would be appreciated.

I had irregular bleeding on jolivette. Three weeks apart, 2 weeks apart, and then no period for the past 8 weeks. After it had been 5 weeks late, I took a pregnancy test just to rule out pregnancy... it was negative. Then a couple weeks after this, I noticed I was extremely tired a lot, lost my appetite, and was feeling a little sick. I honestly thought something else was going on but decided to take another hpt just to be sure. So today... I had 2 positive pregnancy tests! I do not recommend using this "birth control"!

I gave this pill a 5 for effectiveness as it was very effective at what it was supposed to do, prevent pregnancy, its the side effects that are the killer.  I didn't put on any weight or have changes in my skin, the problem was my lack of energy.  by 10:30 every night (which was when I would take the pill) I was exhausted and could barely hold my head up.  I have been off the pill for about 2 months now, and my energy is back, for this reason alone, I wouldn't try femcon.

I have been on Femcon for not even a full two months and decided to stop!  It has caused a terrible rash on my arms and legs, dry contacts, blurred vision.  Since I'm a diabetic it shot my blood sugar up to 300 and I always had control of it.  It's caused strange aches in my legs,feet & ankles.  And piercing temple aches. And beside all this of course I'm bleeding for 10 days, off 3 days and back to bleeding 10 or so days every month.  Supposedly it was to keep my periods down to a minimum!  This drug is the worst thing that ever happened to me! I wouldn't recommend this to anyone!

I was use to using the patch, did great. Now 9 months after having my baby, my dr. started me on femcon. I hate it!!!! I have been bleeding for 11 days. My doctor's nurse says give it time. I am sick and tired of this period. I will be starting my 2nd month of pills,tomorrow, if it doesn't stop soon I will toss them in the trash.
sweating damn it
Experiencing sweating and imbalancr
Gustatory sweating=diabetic

I've been on gianvi for six months and when I got my script from walgreens this month (2 weeks ago) they have me vestura. ... since taking it I've kept these crazy breakouts and I've never ever had acne like my entire life. .I just talked to Wal-Mart pharmacy abd they said they both have same active ingredient but it may be the in active ingredient causing this. . It's embarrassing and they shouldn't be allowed to switch your medicine from a man's brand or generic with out telling you first.

I was on Apri prior to Loryna and thought it was a happy medium from the other "monster pills" I had been on before.  I eventually got tired of the crying so I switched to Loryna.  Best move ever!  Yes, there was a little bit of acne and spotting during the transition, but that's normal.  I feel like I'm back to my old happy self and have not a care in the world.  I was hesitant to switch since there are so many awful reviews that make it online but I couldn't be more pleased!

I have never in my life written a review on anything but I feel so strongly about this drug I feel others should be warned. I was on Gianvi for 2 years and loved it, I meet experienced any side effects from it. My pharmacy switched the Gianvi to loryna and told me it was the same thing but ITS NOT! I've been on it for a couple of months and since starting I've gained 7 lbs and have gotten horrible acne! I have never in my life had acne not even as a teenager and this is awful. I'm a tiny person 5'3 110 lbs and no amount of diet and exercise seems to get rid of the weight I've gained on this bc! As if the weight gain and acne isn't enough I also have been getting very hot and my period comes and goes as it pleases. I also have been bruising all over my legs, i will have at least 20 bruises on legs at one time. I called my dr today and she called in the Gianvi so I am switching ASAP! Awful awful experience with this!

I was switched from Yaz to Loryna after my insurance was switched and the new insurance would not cover Yaz. I had been taking Yaz long term to help control my migraines and it worked great. I was assured Loryna was the same hormones as Yaz with just generic fillers. Impossible. Within the first week on Loryna I had a terrible migraine and started spotting. I had horrible mood swings, zero patience, and anxiety, I was nasty all of the time. I even had dreams where I was being mean and snippy to people! What bothers me the most is that they try to make you think you are taking the same pill, just the generic version, and there is no way the hormones are exactly the same formula as Yaz.

I had good results with Yaz, Beyaz and Gianvi, but when I switched to Loryna as the generic for Yaz, my acne worsened.  I always have mood changes with my period, but the changes to my skin have been terrible in the three pill packs I've been taking it.  Acne disappeared on Yaz, Beyaz and Gianvi.  On Loryna, acne came back with a vengeance.  I've had large cystic acne along my jawline, cheeks and chin since being on Loryna, and I don't understand why doctors and pharmaceutical makers allow this drug to be a substitute for Yaz.  It's ridiculous what we have to put up with as women, the lack of medical attention and solutions to health problems!  Filling out this review in the hopes people will remove this drug from their formularies!!

I've been taking Yaz for over a year now and switched to the generic, Gianvi, in June.  While I've always thought people who claimed generics were different were simply paranoid, I've noticed two subtle differences between the two.

1) I *always* got my period at the same time on the 3rd of sugar pills day taking Yaz.  I now get it slightly later in the day on the 4th day of taking sugar pills.

2) Yaz cleared up my acne completely.  Now I'm scrambling around digging up my old face creams because simply washing my face once a day does not keep it clear.

Decided to try YAZ after my PMS symptoms have started taking over my life 2 weeks every month and I needed relief.  Just after the first pack, I didn't experience many of my normal mental and phsyical PMS symptoms and was very relieved.  I do have mild side effects of nausea and dizziness, but I can handle those better than the long list of PMS symptoms I used to have.

I've been taking Yaz for about ten months in order to treat my PCOS. Therefore I'm not really sure how effective it is in preventing pregnancy since I dont naturally ovulate anyway. For the most part it makes my periods lighter and shorter. Sometimes when I decide to skip I get some spotting which is of course highly annoying. There were only two major side effects that were negative for me. First, my breasts hurt for about a month after I started taking it. Even worse than that was my breasts grew about 2 cup sizes (bad when I was already a 36DD).

I was originally taking Yaz and started experiencing severe adverse effects. The nurse practitioner changed my medication to Mononessa and I have been on it for over 2 years.I cannot be happier. The periods are short, I did not experience weight gain, no babies and absence of ovarian cysts! The only negatives I experience is mild acne and intermittent period pain.I believe that no drug can be perfect for every women, therefore sometimes you must try a few to see what your body prefers. Hope this was helpful.

Quasense works as birth control because you can just forget about having a sex life at all. Instead of 4 periods a year you have several unpredictable periods per year each lasting several weeks each. I would like to thank my insurance company for forcing me to switch to this generic version of seasonale so that that they can save money and I can continue to pay my insurance premiums, the copay for this sorry excuse of a drug and extra feminine hygiene products. I will be changing back to the monthly ones ASAP.
Using Quasense for 4 years. Spotting only first 5 month. No side effects. Would recommend this oral contraceptive to women who would like to take oral contraceptives to eliminate monthly periods.

I only used it for a month and I was extremely unhappy with it. The first day I had to leave school early w/ nausea and throwing up. My face has never broken out as badly as it did when I took Quasense. HORRIBLE. Also, I don't gain weight easily and I gained 6 pounds in the 1 month that I took it. Spotting and lots of discharge everyday. I would not recommend.

My dermatologist prescribed it for excessive sweating.  After years of suffering with this, trying Drysol, the electric current/water devices, etc...  I asked him about Botox.  He suggested we try this first, as he has had good luck with it.  What a difference it's made in my life.  I've been taking it for a little over a year now, and just take one tablet every other day.  The only side affect I've had is my nails tend to get a little brittle sometimes.

This medication makes me sweat profusely! My BP is sometimes good and at other times not so good. BP is very inconsistent with this medication. The water pill additive in this med also makes peeing an every hour thing! I've been on this stuff for over 10 years and do think my body is used to it already and basically rendering it ineffective. Maybe time to ask for a change!

unfortunately after taking this medication..it CLEARED UP THE PROBLEM UNDER MY ARMS...BUT MY BODY FOUND OTHER PLACES TO ELIMINATE SWEAT..LIKE THE RECTAL AREA..AND LEAVES A LINGERING ODOR....i wish i never took this drug...and trying to find a way to reverse this AWFUL EMBARRASING EFFECT..

I am 21 years old, and have been struggling with sweaty palms and feet, FOREVER! This medication is wonderful to help the constant sweaty palms and feet that can be very uncomfortable and somewhat embarrassing. I used it years ago, and recently started using it again. It is really the only thing that helps control the sweaty palms. It can dry out your skin too much, but it is a simple fix. Don't us it as much!

I have had hyperhydrosis since I was a teenager in high school. Made for some wildly uncomfortable experiences. I went through a period of only wearing dark shirts to hide the massive sweat stains. Since using this product, I no longer have to worry, It's a miracle if I sweat at all, even when I'm hot. Word of caution, this product is extremely effective, but can have some side effects. When I first used this product, I experienced an extreme burning sensation under my arms. Blisters even broke out within 2 hrs of application. My doctor suggested I apply it at night after a shower. Keep it on no longer than 2 hrs then wipe it off. It takes 2 applications (2 nights) to get the results I want, but I get it without the blisters and discomfort. I only need to use it 4 times a year (mostly during warmer weather). Definitely changed my life.

I always had problem with armpit sweating. I been using HYPERCARE for about 2 years and i love it! i dont sweat at all. I only apply it every other week now maybe even once a month and i dont sweat. I'm very happy and i'm able to wear nice clothes.. =D!

I have taken this since shortly after having my son because I was nursing.  I am switching now that I'm done.  I used to have a cycle so regular you could set your watch by it...now I think I might be pregnant all the time because of late periods, abdominal pains, nausea, etc.  Like other commentors, I have increased acne, my hair is unmanageable, and suffer mood swings.  This pill does not stop all women from ovulating (me being one of them) and I always worry that I really am pregnant...then I get a 12-14 day period.  

The hair loss that many have experienced is most likely the normal post-partum hair loss.  You lose less while you're pregnant because of the hormones.

My doctor recommended Camilla, or “mini-pill”, since I am currently breastfeeding. I have been on it for almost five months and haven’t had a period; which could be attributed to breastfeeding I suppose! My hair was falling out like crazy for a while, but has calmed down now; however, after being pregnant and giving birth, it’s completely normal for “a ton of hair” to fall out, since pregnant women stop losing hair sometime mid-pregnancy and the body just “plays catch-up” postpartum. So I figure my hair falling out was pregnancy related, not pill related!

Overall I’m happy so far with Camilla, although I assumed I would get regular periods (even without an off week) and had to take a few home pregnancy tests in the beginning for peace of mind…that would be something pharmacists should include with their “make sure you take ALL the pills” comments =) Taking the pill at the same time isn’t too difficult for me, I just take it before bed and if we plan on being out past 9:30 pm, I just grab my pill for that day and take it along.

I hate this pill.  It should be banned.  I have experienced MAJOR HAIR LOSS and blamed my hairdresser after I thought it was from a bad highlight but then he said it's falling out from the root which means it's hormonal; also have white patches all over my stomach.  I have seen these symptoms on other reviews and now know it's from this awful pill.

I started using Camila because other B/C pills made my blood pressure skyrocket! I have been very PLEASED with the pill overall. I enjoyed not having a period for 6 months, however there were a couple pregnancy tests needed.  After the six month mark... my periods and breakthrough bleeding are somewhat frustrating however my periods were never normal so its not a huge change. I have noticed acne on my face which was never a problem prior to the pill. Taking a pill the same time every day isnt so bad...set an alarm people (its just like making it to work on time)!  I guess the biggest plus is that my heart doesnt feel like its beating out of my chest on this pill and that im NOT PREGNANT! I would recommend this pill to most!

I was put on Camila because I'm breastfeeding and haven't had my period in the 5 months I've been on it.  No apparent side effects (noticeable hair loss, but I've attributed to post-pregnancy).  Will likely stay on it until I'm done breastfeeding in a few months.

I was taking Camrese because my periods were extremely painful, and as BC once I started having sex. Insurance switched me to Amethia and it is horrible. Depression symptoms, bloating and cramps for a month, and hand tremors.

I have been taking seasonique for 3 months and a week and I love it! I haven't had any of the side effects I am seeing. No spotting, no acne, no moodiness. I went on this pill because YAZ was getting way to expensive and I wanted one period a season. Who wouldn't? All I can say is give it a whirl. Unfortunately, I have been getting persistent yeast infections from being on seasonique. My third so far. Apparenly this doesn't seem to be a common side effect because I cant find n e complaints about it. Other than that, the pack is too bulky to carry in a small purse. I've learned today that loseasoniqe is much cheaper, and is the same as seasonique. it just comes in monthly perscriptions... I wish I would have known b4 but maybe i can help save some of you money on this.

I have used this drug for many years, switching from seasonique due to the cost. I love it but, I experience breakthru bleeding from time to time. I found that when it starts, I just stop takin the pills and let the cycle complete and once it is over, usually like 4days later i jus start back takin the pills. If u keep takin them while bleeding even if it is just a little, it will carry on longer. But over all I like the pills

I started on Seasonique because of the 4 periods a year. I'm on week 7 and have had some spotting or bleeding for 4 of 7 weeks. I have had stomach ache,diarrhea, and a lack of sex drive. I've given this pill a chance, but I don't think it's worth taking.

I took Seasonique for a couple years before a generic came out.  The first generic I was first given Camrese.  The first packed worked great and for $10 I couldn't beat it.  Seasonique was $55 so I was thrilled with the much cheaper alternative.  Then 2nd pack of Camrese was terrible.  I had a period almost every single day for 3 months.  Terrible cramping and much heavier flow than when I was on Seasonique.  I was going to switch back to the name brand but though I would try it one more time.  The 3rd generic pack the pharmacy gave me was Amethia.  Thought it was worth a try.  Amethia, for me, has been wonderful.  My periods which normally lasts about 2 solid weeks was only a couple days and no break through bleeding or periods at the wrong time.  I've had almost no cramping with Amethia which for me is a miracle.

I'm taking this for multiple reasons. Started with seasonique for the first three months loved it. Then was switched to amethia, first pack was ok, then the spotting happened and from reading all the other comments on here glad I'm not alone. Also headaches I've had could be due to this. Loved the price but not worth the worry of when bleeding (which was more like clots for me) will end. So going back to seasonique, maybe the other generic which is exactly the same. Hated Amethia!!!!

I did not experience any spotting with Amethia (which shocked me since Mirena made me spot constantly). The only major side effect I noticed was that my acne flaired up, worse than when I went through puberty. I went today to see my NP and she said the higher levels of testosterone leads to this side effect. I did not gain weight or experience mood swings. I decided to switch because the acne was so bad.

I have experienced a decrease in the intensity of my hot flashes.  I've gained 20lbs in the month and a half since I starting using this patch.  The patch itches and burns and leaves a rash.  I've only used it on my upper buttock.  I am afraid to place it on my stomach.

Worked well for treating hot flashes. I spotted for a few days, but after using the patch for 2 1/2 months no other bleeding. Have however felt nauseated and have had some deep abdominal pain. Hope this will pass. Have not heard many people talk about stomach issues other than weight gain.

I am 52 and have used this patch for 17 years due to total hysterectomy.  Started on .1, but had breast tenderness so changed to .075.  This has worked great for me in the past but have developed terrible migraines the day after putting on a new patch due to hormone surge.  I will be trying oral pill in hopes of controlling migraine.

topics.top_condition: Low Estrogen After Operation to Remove Ovaries
example_quotes: I have been on the Vivelle Dot for years and years. I had a complete hysterectomy in 1986.I feel great. No symptoms of menopause. Hope to stay on it for ever!

I have been on vivelle dot for 21 years after a complete hysterectomy at the age of 25 years old due to severe fibroid tumors.They removed all my parts including ovaries. I started HRT patch right after my operation. It has stopped the hot flashes but I still have mood swings and I have gained alot of weight, wasn't sure if it was middle age. I am 46 years old now, but after reading others reviews for this drug, it makes me wonder if it has been this drug! I apply a patch once a week due to the expensive price. It seems to keep the hot flashes away as long as I have one on, but if I go without for more than 2 weeks. I start getting continuous hot flashes and irritability. My Dr wants me to get off of them due to the long time I have been on them due to my long term use and the health risks to me, but I feel like I still need them to control my menopausal symptoms and stay sane! I'm still trying to decide whats next for me. are there Any natural treatments that will help??

I have been on Vivelle dot for almost 1 year.  I am in perimenopause and experienced hot flashes, cold flashes, crashing fatigue, painful intercourse, crying and generally feeling like I was losing my mind.  The medication stopped all those symptoms. I am on .05 and am thinking of stopping or going to a lower dose.  I'm afraid of long term effects and I'm experiencing weight gain.  I've recently felt somewhat lightheaded as well.  All in all I give this med 5 stars.  It was a life saver for me.

I'm 31 and have been taking Tri Sprintec for 11 months now for birth control and to keep my periods regulated. The cramps are still present but are better than when not on a pill. I have little to no sex drive which is negatively affecting my relationship as well as moodiness.  Things easily set me off and the bad mood is hard to come out of. Sex is uncomfortable due to dryness 3 out of the 4 weeks. I haven't gained weight but I do notice I am intaking more calories in week 3 than the other weeks -- thankfully I work out often. I will most likely ask to switch pills to see if another might work for me better. Overall, it is better than past pills but I still don't think I've found the right one yet.

I have been on Tri-Cyclen for just over 6 months now. When I started taking the pill I felt nauseous, had constant headaches, and felt extremely sad. The sadness and other side effects for the most part have diminished until recently. I can't go more than 4 hours without crying or feeling upset. I have incredibly awful mood swings and get angry at the smallest things, where I will throw things or scream at people. This pill has been amazing for preventing pregnancy, clearing the bulk of my acne, and reducing cramps, however, the sadness that I am feeling on this pill is unbearable. I have constant suicidal thoughts and it's not worth it anymore. Hopefully this pill will work for you, but unfortunately it did not work for me. (Side note: I am not depressed/felt this way before taking this pill)

I was on Trinessa for almost a year but went off of it for six months. Now I'm back on and taking Tri-sprintec and have been for almost a year now.
Pros - Effective birth control, cleared up my acne amazingly, and made my body more "womanly"

Cons - Moodiness, depression, irrational outbursts, menstrual cramps, longer and heavier periods, very decreased sex drive (which kinda defeats the purpose doesn't it?)

I would go with something else.. but I have a feeling anything else involving hormones would effect me the same way. It's working how it's supposed to, So.. call me complacent.

I've been taking Sprintec for a year now. I used to have periods that would be extremely heavy and could last up to 2 weeks at a time. I would also end up with a cold about a week or so before my period was to start. 
Now my periods last maybe 5 days at the most, and are very very light- so I'm a happy camper! Only issue I've had is that I do get cramps now the first (which I didn't get before the pill)...only lasts about 1/2 a day though and seems to be getting better every month. Other than that small thing, this pill's been very good to me :)
i have been on 2 other pills in the past and neither one of them worked even half as good as sprintec! no weight can...no cramping at all anymore! the major plus is my boobs got bigger...lol

I have been taking Sprintec for a year and for the most part I have been happy with it.  It did help clear up my acne, and thus far it has prevented pregnancy.  However, I do experience a lot of spotting and tend to get yeast infections more frequently.  Also, it doesn't really help with reducing cramps.

I was diagnosed last year with PCOS and was just perscribed this medicine today.  I look forward to the weight loss but mainly hopefully getting pregnant.  I havent filled the prescription yet, any advice??

ParaGard has been effective in preventing pregnancy so far. I've had it in for about 7 weeks. I did experience excruciating pain during insertion (felt like a heavy lead pipe was being suspended parallel by only my uterus). Awful, but fleeting. I was nauseous and dizzy for about 15 minutes and then it subsided. The biggest side effects have been much heavier periods (reminiscent of my teenage years) with increased cramping. I went from a 4 day period, with only two medium-heavy days (on the pill) to 7-8 day periods with 5-6 very heavy days. And my periods have been more frequent than they ever were.
The first month, I had a surge in the amount of discharge present, but that has stopped. I have also been spotting between cycles, which had decreased with time. 
Background: I switched from the pill to the NuvaRing (which I hated) and back to the pill, which then began to give me severe side effects, including high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, decreased libido, anxiety and depression (YES, all of that!). I ceased taking the pill mid-cycle, and it has taken these 7 weeks to get back to my regular 26-day cycle, so I don't blame the ParaGard entirely for the irregularity. 
Overall, I have been pleased. The absense of any serious side-effects associated with hormones makes the longer, heavier cycles worth it. And I expect that they will decrease, based on the reviews of others and my doctor's input. I do not plan to have it in for 10 years (I'm recently married and plan to have children within 2 years), I just needed a hassle-free, safe method. I hope the removal doesn't hurt as much as the insertion, but now I know to take 1-2 Motrin (and maybe a muscle relaxer) before the appointment. I hope this review is helpful!

example_quotes: I used this drug to soften my cervix prior to iud insertion after a previous attemted insertion failed because my doctor could not get my cervix to open.  It worked.

Although this medication was effective for controlling/preventing postpartum hemorrhage, I had a very weird reaction to it. After the intramuscular injection in the hospital I felt very strange. Almost as if I was out of my body. Difficult to explain but   I very much did not feel like myself at all.  I chalked it up though to just the excitement and exhaustion after giving birth. About 6 to 8 hours later I finally felt "normal" again. Two weeks later I began to experience some gushing bleeding so I was prescribed some Methergine tablets. After the first tablet I had the same bizarre feelings. I could not wait for it to get out of my body so I could feel back to myself again. Twenty years earlier I had taken this same medication for some postpartum bleeding and had no side effects whatsoever at that time. After this last time and my freaky reaction I will not ever take this drug again unless my life depended on it.

I was 16 weeks pregnant when I found out the baby had died at 14 weeks. The baby was too large for my body to pass the body naturally. I had to use two pills and insert them into my vagina then 2 hours before the surgery I had to insert two more. I experienced no bleeding but I had painful contractions in my back and stomach. This medication was used to soften my cervix making it safer and easier to dialate my cervix without any tears. It was sucsessful.

I started taking Zyprexa for a bipolar diagnosis.  Made me very ill for the first few weeks.  Required hospitalization. severe vomiting with serious abdominal pain. The only benefit of this drug was knocking me out at night to make me sleep.

I started taking zyprexa about 8 months ago and I have gained about 50 pounds and I have no energy and I am pretty sure I'm on the verge of getting diabetes. It has helped a bit with the symptoms though. Overall it is not worth the side effects.

Hi: I am looking to hear from others who have had similar bad side efx.  I started taking zyprexa in '99 (to the present day) for years of sleep deprivation, wasn't feeling myself, etc. It soon started to help me sleep & dream (REM) -- which was nice, although I did gain 50 pounds in a year or 2.  Around 2001, I began having trouble with stuttering (speech) -- talking is extremely difficult now; sleep apnea (I go into respiratory arrest while asleep and have to tell myself to breathe/inhale when I wake up with oxygen deprivation in my brain--feels like a near death experience); and also some numbness/stroke like symptoms.

I would love to hear from anyone who has experienced any similar (neurological) symptoms while on zyprexa.  I would also LOVE to file a lawsuit against Eli Lilly for damages, but getting medical & scientific proof linking the zyprexa to the symptoms I experience is difficult, if not impossible.

BTW.....here's a pharmaceutical cost tidbit for you.  When I started taking zyprexa in 1999, it cost $6.00 per tablet (retail).  Twelve years later, it now costs $15.00 per tablet retail....thank goodness for insurance, but just goes to show how much Eli Lilly loves to profit from this.  Also, in case you haven't heard, the patent on zyprexa expires in 2012.

Please feel free to contact me at: [EMAIL_REDACTED] thanks. :)

I began taking Lexapro when Zoloft stopped working for me. My friend was on lexapro and said she loved it; I on the other hand had other problems. I was adamant against trying an anti-depressant after having a terrible experience with zoloft in 1999. I tried the lexapro and I can't believe how much better I feel and my performance at work shows. I've been on 20 mg a couple weeks now, a few jitters but feel like i'm adjusting to the new dosage.

After trying Zoloft for a month and feeling worse on it, my doctor prescribed me Lexapro. Every day for a week, I had a debilitating headache like I have never had before. The headaches would last for hours. Hopefully whatever I try next will work - third time is the charm, right?
I didn't get pregnant so thats good!

I have been breastfeeding for 7months and it seems to be okay...except the fact I have to use drain-o all the time because of my hair falling out...by the way i could sweep my bathroom floor everyday.
so far i am not preggo

It's apparently effective, as I have not gotten pregnant, but I have nearly every side effect. I'm very angry, and I am getting the iud removed ASAP.
After being on Wellbutrin for a few weeks ,with no help, my dr prescribed Zoloft.So far I have felt wonderful.I have more energy and seem more happy about things.Its working wonderful for me.

I read all of the posts and found some that I could definately identify with.  I've been on Wellbutrin SR for almost 2 months.  I transitioned to this from Zoloft (taken on and off for 3-4 years).  I switched because Zoloft drastically increased my appetite and I began gaining weight.  I have had some improvements on Wellbutrin including: weight loss, increased energy, getting out of bed much easier, return of sex-drive, and more motivation.  I did have insomnia when I started the Wellbrutrin.  That has gone and I actually think I'm sleeping better than I have in years.  I have also experienced some minor upset stomach from time to time, slightly shaky hands, and weird/stressful dreams.  The only concerns I have are that I am starting to feel a little paranoid and I tear up extremely easily.  I haven't started any uncontrollable crying but I'm afraid I might.  I am having monthly check-ups with my doctor so I can voice my concerns.  I also think it is very beneficial to seek out the help of a psychologist/psychiatrist.  Overall I am pleased with the progress.  I'm very close to finishing up a PhD and this has greatly improved my productivity and motivation.
After trying Wellbutrin and Zoloft with no luck this drug is wonderful.I have more energy and its helping me with controlling my weight.I feel so much better:)

The celexa has been very helpful with the suicidal thoughts and the depression, the only things that bother me is I find it very hard to cry and like one of the other reviews I read, I feel numb.  I've only gained 2 pounds and this I believe is from the holiday eating as I've been on the med since September 2007 and just gained the weight in December. I really never had calmness like I do now on the celexa.  I've been on paxil and gained 50 pounds, on wellbutrin and lost weight but never on anything that has helped me this much. Citalopram has worked for Me. I noticed the changes in my behavior immediately; like within the first 2 and a half weeks. I no longer cried as much. I've tried energy drinks and I eat very healthy foods, but it doesn't last very long. Its weird, but 
I STILL would recommend Celexa to anyone suffering from any form of Depression!
I have taken Celexa for 2 years and changed to Sertaline 3 weeks ago. It seems to give me more energy and I feel a lot better! No side effects for me. I take it in the morning.

I have taken limbrel for 2 days now, and the pain has gotten worse.  I have been running a fever, and very tired.  After reading some of the reviews I am going to stop taking it and see if the fever goes away.  Will make a review again in a couple of days to see if it is better.

First of all, I am a very healthy person that happens to have osteoarthritis as a function of my age. After a certain time using Limbrel I developed an unexplainable fever accompanied by chills,body aches,nausea,and fatigue. I had to be hospitalized for 4 days and received 3 units of blood for extreme anemia. The anemia could not be explained, neither could the blood in my stool. After an upper and lower GI work-up nothing significant could be found to explain the blood loss. People should be aware that Limbrel can cause all these side effects. I am 100% better after discontinuing the drug. The slight improvement I found to my osteoarthritis is not worth the terrible way Limbrel made me feel in general.

After three months of severe pain in my hands for which the orthopedist prescribed steroids followed by NSAIDS (my pain continued with higher and lower intensity throughout the three months of treatment), I decided to see a rheumatologist.  He prescribed Limbrel.  It is definitely a miracle drug and my pain went from a severe 10 to no pain within 48 hours.  
The first day I took the medication my stomach was very upset, however, within 3 days the stomach pains decreased and by the fourth day, I felt perfect.  I have been taking Limbrel for a month, I have no stomach issues, no pain in my hands and I work in front of a computer, typing, an average of 12 to 14 hours a day.
I like how its not as big as most prenatal vitamins

I used this vitamin while I was pregnant and now that I've been breast feeding for a year and it's great!!!! No nausea, no problems taking it on an empty stomach and it's easy to swallow.   I would definitley reccomend this prenatal vitamin.  The ingredients are truly a complete compliment.

When I became pregnant my physician switched my High blood pressure medicine to Procardia XL as it was safer in pregnancy than the Norvasc and the HCTZ. It worked very well. I took one pill/day. I liked this a lot.  I used this instead of prenatal's which made me sick.

CONCERNED and Scared....Zoloft kept me level, even...now Zoloft causing high anxiety..since was on Prozac 7 weeks. Stopped Prozac due to high anxiety...Just switched back to Zoloft..

I have been o Zoloft for over 2 years now. Before Zoloft I had tried many different meds, none worked as well as zoloft does. I take 200mg everyday and another medicine for anxiety it's grerat being independant again and able to hold down a job and take care of my child like a mom should. before I found Zoloft my life was a mess it's still one day at a time but it is well worth it. as far as side effects go I did notice headaches some in the begining but over time side effects went away. I don't ever want to change meds again. Zoloft is not for everyone just like prozac wasn't for me it made me ill and mean if you Zoloft is right for you you will be able to tell i think within a month of being on it it was like night and day after i got to full strength dosage. I took 25mg once a day for treatment of post-partum depression. It worked well for helping my mood, but it strongly affected my desire to have sex. My depression worsened six months into treatment due to extreme psychological trauma. The doctor increased my dose to 50 mg. I experienced my first ever manic episode at 30 years old. I have been free from psychiatric medication for three years. Unfortunately, a steroid used for treating H1N1 induced a brief manic period in me as well. No more Zoloft for me now but bipolar disorder for life. I don't blame the Zoloft, though. Even though I hadn't had any other mood episodes, BPD runs in my family. I think the Zoloft just helped it come to the surface.

I took Zoloft for 22 years for MDD/panic disorder. Stopped working when I started going through menopause 3 years ago. I have tried, what seems like, every combo of meds since. I have taken this for 1 week so far. Some nausea, nothing else. Keeping my fingers crossed.

I have been taking Zoloft to treat anxiety/panic attacks for 5 months now. Overall I am very happy with the medication. When I was first diagnosed I was put on Celexa, which had very undesirable side effects in which I couldn't even function to do anything during the day I was a zombie, however, after switching to Zoloft, I have had no side effects, and my panic attacks have since dissappeared after 2 weeks of starting the meds. I would definitly recommend this for anyone suffering from a similar condition!
