I have cronic fatigue with fibromyalgia. this make me alert and active all day!
Using for both fibromyalgia and anxiety, and the headaches that accompany anxiety. Wonderful that it works for all conditions, the pain has virtually disappeared.
Been taking for several years for Ankylosing Spondylitis.  Also, take Omeprazole for stomach.

I have taken Robaxin  twice now and each time it works great for me and my back pain, it seems to stop my back getting worse and within 24 hours I am back to fully fit again.
I have only taken Robaxin for 6 days and it has eased my muscle pain

DOXYCYCL HYC EATS ME ALIVE BUT I NEED TO  TAKE  IT FOR A YEAR. MY DR GAVE  ME  PROCHLORPER MALEATE. IT ALSO STOP THE OF I AM GOING YOU DIE FEELING, YOU KNOW LAYING IN BED ALL DAY FEELING SICK. NOW IT GOING TO BE A GREAT YEAR.

I wast happy about that but if I wanted to function, & I had to be able to move with a severly ADHD child, I had to take them. Over next few yrs I developed a tolerance & the pills just didnt help as much. I was started on Kadian & it has been a god sent. I take 60mg in am & 60mg at bedtime. The best part is I dont have the side effects such as grogginess etc. that comes with narcotics. The down side to Kadian is the expense! Without my insurance 60 pills would cost me $597.00 each month.
Kadian is a great medicine, but the capsules are hard to swallow and to keep down for me.

I have neurofibromatosis, and have as many as 50 fibromas (tumors) up and down my spine. The several that are in my lumbar spine are the ones that cause me the most of my pain. In the morning prior to taking my medication the pain scale is at 10. After about 30 minutes of taking the medicine the scale drops to about 5. The effectiveness problem is partially due to the fact that I have been on this same dose for over 2 years. My doctor added Kadian to my treatment in order to keep me from having to take the Lortab more than 4 times a day. I have been on augmentation thearpy for over a year and have found that it works for my condition extremely well and my quality of life has improved since starting it last year. I would definately recommend this medication and the staff of Nurses that administer it nationwide.

Have chronic sinusitis so when I developed my annual fall sinus infection, the doctor put me on this. Aside from the stomach upset, I developed a mild burning sensation/funny taste in my mouth after the second day of use, and my face broke out in a horrible rash.

I had a pimple on my eyebrow which turned nastier and infected the surrounding areas including my cheek. The doctor prescribed Augmentin.  Normally all antibiotics I have taken have had no side effects. Within a day of taking Augmentin I was violently sick, for two days. I persevered till the end but during that week felt listless, stomachy and ate meals although I didn't feel like them. I will certainly inform my doctor of my experience when I visit him again.
Good for lowering blood pressure but am diabetic and my glucose levels have risen.  Dr. won't change med because he believes Micardis is better for kidneys.

I have gained weight within the first 3 weeks and after the 3rd week I found myself extremely irritable.  It does help me sleep but my irritable moods outweigh the advantages of sleeping for 4 hours.
Weight Gain- Sleep too much   Cannot deal with either with diabetes and a 92 yr old mother with alzheimer in my care
has controled my ansiety, sleeplesness, and weight gain.

I have gotten Ketamine injections and this creme mixed with ketamine RX by my pain dr. It's Useless. The creme lasts maybe 30 minutes. I have Fibromyalgia, Degenerative Disc Disease, Stenosis and migraines.

Now I'm on levaguin, a more potent antibiotic.

Two days after taking just one pill, the pain has spread throughout my whole body, the worst of it being in my low back and legs, similar to Sciatica.  I have painful headache and constant ringing in my ears.  I canâ??t sleep and I am afraid to take any pain killers or sleep aids as I am terrified it will make my condition worst.  I pray that I do not have long term side effects like prior reviews I have read.  I took one pill and stopped and two days later the pain is getting worst!  Never never never take Levaquin.  This stuff is poison!

Both my mother and my mother-in-law were given this drug for UTI with dire results. My mother by the 3rd day developed EXTREME TREMORS, so bad she couldn't walk period and couldn't feed herself or do anything else without help. Two yrs. later my mother-in-law called us in the dead of night with wild heart palpitations, even with a pacemaker, faint, etc. Called hospital to see if we should bring her in & they said CALL 911 NOW! In the meantime I asked her if she was taking any new medications & then checked which antibiotic she was taking... Lo & Behold, it was Levaquin. At the hospital I told them I thought it was the Levaquin & they said, oh no, couldn't be, that's too rare. So after EKGs, bloodwork, & x-rays, they came in & said she was having a reaction the Levaquin !!! If it's so rare, how do I know 2 people, personally, that had very bad reactions to it?

I had what turned out to be systemic pneumococcal complicated with severe bronchitis and body-wide infections and inflammation. I suffered with this for 8 weeks before my doctor prescribed 500mg of Levaquin (Levofloxacin). My symptoms before this already included severe sudden onset arthritic-like joint pains (every joint), muscle pains, sinus pains, sinus headaches, severe and very swollen sore throat, hoarseness, painful earaches with drainage, very scratchy and irritation in upper chest when breathing, infection and inflammation of pericardium sac causing accumulation of fluid which caused it to look like heart was enlarged on x-ray, pleurisy, etcetera.

While on the Levaquin, my symptoms began clearing up slowly but surely. Unfortunately at the end of the cycle most symptoms were still present. Better, but not cured.

My doctor would prescribe anymore antibiotics (he seemed to not understand that pneumococcal is / can be more than "just pneumonia") and  referred me to an Infectious Disease doctor who could see me in late February 2016 (this was now early December 2015). 

Things very rapidly relapsed and worsened. A few days before Christmas I was at the Urgent Care where I saw a Nurse Practitioner was on duty) and then the doctor - he was shocked that this had been allowed to get this bad (by my doctor). He initially considered admitting me for IV ADMINISTRATION OF ANTIBIOTICS. Instead he prescribed me 750mg of Levaquin for a 10-day cycle. The stronger dose of Levaquin has clearly been of a stronger, quicker response to this bacterial infection. 

Also, the NP referred me to a study of over 7500 people in a Clinical Trial on this drug listed on RxList. 4.3% of participants dropped out due to adverse responds (most minor). Serious reactions were less that 0.01% of participants. Also about 1996 Dutch study that tracked 318,000 Levaquin prescriptions and after a year found less than 15 cases of tendon ruptures that MAY be associated. All responded to rehab

I read a lot of negative reviews on here before taking the medication, and overall had a positive experience so I wanted to share. I was still spiking a low grade fever nearly every day and still wasnâ??t feeling great. My doc prescribed me 500mg of levo for 7 days  and that seemed to have done the trick. Struggling through a respiratory sickness for 12 days, I visited my Dr. to make sure I did not have strep, pneumonia, or something else. The next day I felt like I had been in a car accident, and the day after that I am still moving at the pace of a turtle--in much aching discomfort in neck, knees, upper arms, hip.  I DO NOT recommend this drug.  If you need an antibiotic, ask for something else.  Side effects:  Insomnia both nights after taking drug. Third and fourth days (drug not taken those days) had bad neck stiffness, arthritis in my knees was badly aggravated.   Appetite greatly suppressed.  Constipation.

My 78 yo father has been taking 20 mg of Lasix close to two weeks & is now getting side effects such as:  Increased Thirst, Have trouble sleeping, can not stand up, can not hear at times, is loosing weight.

Have been taking 10mg dose for several months. In the beginning it did a good job of controlling my blood pressure with no other side effects. Now I am experiencing a few. Considerable swelling of ankles and feet are the biggest concern now. Sometimes I feel bloated, like I'm retaining fluid. I urinate almost every hour all night long. Tough to get a good nights rest. My sex drive is almost zero. (yes there is sex after sixty :) Oh, and my ears itch. Strange, but true. My blood pressure is still good (115-120 over 75) But I know I have gained at least 10-15 lbs of water weight. Is there a diuretic pill that can be taken with this drug to counteract the fluid retention? I feel like a water balloon!

I have diastolic dysfunction (stiff heart) and started to have edema in my legs that gradually worsened along with shortness of breath. My doctor started me off with 20mg, then 40mg and now I'm on 80mg Lasix once daily. I finally have ankles, can wear my rings and some shoes. the only serious concerning side effects were my blood glucose shot up to 120mg/dl fron 90mg/dl and elevated my BUN (kidney function). quadrapalegia patient has blood pressure extremely high or very low. When does Norvasc peak for most effectiveness. Drug is taken once daily in the evening. Please help.

I've taken Norvasc 5mg since 9/07/2010.It's now 09/25/2010.On 09/10/10 Dr told me to double to 10mg.Still no change in bp.Avg 150/95.I don't believe they know what they're treating.I've always struggled with way too low BP avg 70/55. [NAME_REDACTED], awoke with extremely swollen ankles & legs..4x in size. Have had 4 back surgeries in 3 years (2 fusions in lower back). Siadic nerve was damaged when my first disc ruptured on it. Now I have "foot drop" after 4th surgery. I have been on Neurontin since 1st surgery. Up to 1200mg 3 times/day. If I miss a dose, the stinging/tingling/bee-sting feelings are so intense, it is unbearable.  I love this drug!
I am prescribed neurontin/gabapentin for chronic pain, and it's been working great for 3 years!

I have idiopathic progressive polyneuropathy, fibromyalgia and osteoarthritis: for the most part the neurontin has been a God-send.  Most of the time, it controls the pain pretty well.  The pain in my feet was horrible, I could only describe it as what the princess and the pea must have experienced--the least little thing that I stepped on would send me through the roof.   There are days when I'm still in A LOT of pain and have to take additional meds.  The down side is that if I forget to take my pills when I'm suppose to, or I've gone out of town and don't have  enough and have to go several days without the neurontin, the pain and burning sensations are exacerbated to an unreal level. I have gained five pounds since I started taking Contrave. I am now on four pills a day and it is not helping with my appetite. I am hungry and my stomach growls. This is when I tend to overeat. Like I did when I was pregnant. I HATE it. I was hoping this would help. I also feel no side-effects. I think if anything I am less blah. I feel a little more upbeat.

I started taking Contrave yesterday a.m. April 17th. I was doing OK until around 6 p.m. I ate a salad with ranch dressing and almost immediately became sick to my stomache. By 9 p.m. I was vomiting everything I ate and almost considered going to the ER. I thought maybe I was coming down with something or ate something bad so I took the pill again this morning. I had 1/2 blueberry muffin and coffee, within an hour I was vomiting again. I called my doctor and was told to stop taking Contrave and call her on Wednesday to let her know how I am doing. I had issues in the beginning with constipation as have many, but I take a high quality probiotic daily and that takes care of the issue. Dry mouth is also pretty bad, so I just drink tons of water to combat that.

can not go without it tried after two days I am to tired to walk or to think I think it it is a live saver!!!

Started with PCP suggesting MS Contin as alternative to the long list of drugs that were tried and had failed.  My neuropathy gives me a pain rating of 5 to 9, on a 24/7 basis.  The 30mg dose, 3 times daily, actually reduced the pain rating by 2 or 3 on the hgih end, and with Lortab for breakthrough, we had finally found a drug that, though not perfect, did better than anything else in the formulary.  After a few years, the effectiveness lowered, and the PCP doubled the dose to 60mg x 3, and 4 years later, again I reported overall pain levels increasing, and at that time, one year ago, she raised the dose to 100mg x 3.  I was hesitant to accept this last doseage increase, as the respiratory system can be depressed with opioid use, and breathing has always been high on my list of things to do.  However, with pain that can be so severe that I would be brought to tears many times a day, and unable to sleep for mone than an hour or two at a time, I did take the increase.  Each time, after a short adjustment period when I felt the "euphoric" side effects, that part went away, and the MS-C went back to doing an adequate job of reducing the severity of my pain.  My advice:  Don't ask for increases in doseage.  Stick  with describing the pain you are feeling, and allow your PCP to determine the best way to handle it.  If you have a good doctor who is familiar with your problem(s), and is sensitive to the same, he/she help  you decide how to best manage your pain.

I get motion sickness even going a movie that has a lot of motion.  Bonine works great in all circumstances for me. (movie, car, boat)As long as I am active it does not make me sleepy.  If I settle in and stay to still it will relax me.

Skelaxin goes right to the pain in both legs and upper arms from multiple herniated discs in back and neck.  I take it as prescribed. That's  the key.

I also have one on my ankle but I have had no response to the cream on my ankle lesion. Three more weeks to go. Good to read other's responses, misery loves company.

My dermatologist prescribed Aldara as a supplement to surgical treatment (biopsy, then additional shaving and cautery) for superficial squamous cell carcinoma on my hand. She told me to use it nightly, beginning 5 days after my surgery ( the surgical site was not yet healed). By night 6 of nightly usage, I had to discontinue the Aldara because of severe, burning pain that kept me awake. I still have the burning at day 8. 

I am concerned that this may have caused nerve damage, although it is early to draw any conclusions. I would not recommend this product, and I certainly would not prescribe it ( I am a physician).

I had a small spot on my neck and started applying Aldara about four weeks ago. It is now about 1.5 in, scabby and it hurts. It is an open sore, skin is tight, burning sensation and I have been nauseaous.  Not sure if that is direct cause or not. I am hopeful it will do its job, but this is difficult to look at and uncomfortable. Wearing a lot of turtlenecks to hide the sore which also irritates the skin.  Trying to be optimistic - I go back to the doctor in 4 more weeks.
topical application to moles or warts -drys them up; decreases size until dried pieces flake off and now down to a surface brown spot instead of a 1/4 diameter brown lump.

also it has been 2 years since I was diagnosed with genital warts and that is when I started using Aldara. I only had to use a couple of weeks, and have had one minor outbreak since. I would recommend this to anyone..

I noticed a comment here posted in August 2015 that I feel compelled to respond to the post with a note of caution.  The poster said they took only a single pill that resulted in a very negative way for them.  I'm of the opinion that the effectiveness of this or any other drug cannot be accurately evaluated after having taken only a single dose of the drug. Have had Crohn's diagnosis for around 8 years, (but probably had it for 15 years before diagnosis) nothing had worked although i would have periods of remission. Cimzia has been a miracle. Other symptoms remain same but you learn to handle or get used to them adjusting what works best for your daily routines and diet. Also due to my breathing difficulties with two blood clots in the lung, Warfarin treated those. There have been intermittent times that I've had to take as much as 80mgs of it, although I did get a little puffy-faced and bloated it wasn't horrible. I did have lots of mood changes but that was worth it considering before I took it I couldn't get out of bed, take a shower, opening anything was impossible and I needed help eating and changing my clothes. Mind you, I was only 27 at the time of my first flare up and 28 at the second. Both were hell, so I'll deal with the side effects of maybe being a little nutty or maybe in the future needing a hip replacement because right now my quality of life is waaay better. Today for the first time I got a test reading that my sedimentation rate was ZERO...totally awesome. 
  So, in short, listen to what your body's telling you, eat right, drink lots of water and get rest when you can. Be prepared to be moody and have trouble sleeping for a bit while you adjust.  Ps. There was someone on here talking about fibromyalgia, I would suggest having them do an ANA work up to see if you have Lupus.

The only complication I worry about is the unknown effect it has on pregnancy. I had a very healthy baby boy prior to my use of enbrel, but after about a year of using enbrel I found out I was pregnant. Thinking I was playing it safe, I stopped using Enbrel (and all other medications, being only darvocet at the time) as soon as I found out I was expecting. 5 months into the pregnancy I had a stillbirth with the cause being unknown.

Before trying Enbrel I used almost all over the counter as well as Rx topicals for my scalp and nothing was helping. Now my head doesnt itch and my psoriasis is clearing up. The only down side is that my legs have bruised from the injections but that's a small very small price to pay for the relief.

I have had very painful psoriatic arthritis in my feet to the point of barely being able to stand or walk.  Also severe psoriasis all over. I have started taking Enbrel with Methotrexate for the past month and 1/2 and have had amazing results.  The swelling and pain are gone and my skin is finally starting to clear up.  I'm so happy to be able to walk without crutches again.  Overall I have had a great experience with Enbrel.  Like others, I hope my insurance company continues to cover the cost because there is no way I could afford it otherwise.
I have been using arava drug since 2006, I think it is a miracle drug.  It helps me to move around and take care of myself.
Switched from MTX to arava...saved me from significant hair loss.  One week of nausea then no adverse side effects.  Great option but must monitor liver enzymes just like with MTX

I HAVE BEEN ON THIS SHOT FOR YEARS AND IT HAS HELPED ME A LOT. NOW THE DR'S HAVE STARED ME ON ARANESP AND I FEEL TERRRIBLE. COULD YOU PLEASE TELL ME IF THIS MED IS A LOT DIFFERENT THAN EPOGEN?   THANK YOU, MARIE

I've had RA since I was 21 (I'm 36, now).  Humira does give a little relief,  but not enough to make life enjoyable again.  The fatigue, flu-like feeling, stomach aches, swelling, joint pain, etc. are all still there.  I've tried all of the medications available for RA, and none have worked with any better results.  I did come back to Humira, because the side-effects were less with Humira than any other drug.  Right now, I only take Humira - nothing with it (like Methotrexate or Arava) mainly because of the side-effects and the fact that they just make me feel worse, not better.  All in all, Humira is better than anything else available; it's just not a cure-all.  I also must say that taking Humira DID NOT prevent me from having multiple surgeries, so slowing joint damage - I'm not convinced of.

Took it July 2008 on the recommendation of
my Rheumatologist. Also being treated for RA
with Humira. That works great. The blood tests (RF ESR etc showed a major improvement).Taking Reclast was the worst decision I ever made. It brought back the RA symptoms in full force
much worse than ever. Extreme bone,muscle and joint pains began about 2 months after the infusion and it's still there now.
I now need Pregnisone, mobic etc.
Don't know if the Humira works anymore as 
the blood tests showed a severe RA flareup two months after the Reclast infusion and it's still there. Hope the Reclast finally wears off.
To those who have RA, think very carefully before considering Reclast.

I cannot type anymore.

Hello, I was diagnosed with RA when I was 28 I'm now 33.  This is a horrible disease and I wish there was more awareness.  Most people don't realize how different RA is from Arthritis. It took 5 months before Humira started working for me.  It allows me to do simple things like walk, get up from chairs, and do small things around the house.  I am far from normal on this drug but I don't know that any drug would put me where a normal 33 year old would be. I take the 40mg shot weekly not the normal every two weeks.  I got pneumonia for the first time in my life over the winter.  I had to take (2) 1 week doeses of Levaquin to get rid of the pneumonia and it took 2.5 months to finally get better because of the Humira. So there are risks involved with all these immune suppressing drugs, but the benefits far out weigh the cons for me.  I have to be able to walk. I have a 7 year old that has to be taken care of.  I pray for a cure for this disease.
Humira has been a good match for me.  I have done well on it, about 2007

I am very please with the resutls of this med. I have been on it for over 3 months now and I have seen a major disappearance of scales. I have smooth skin! I can see and feel my elbows and knees!!! I wish to thank the co-worker who recommended Humira to me. I can wear shorts again! (Living in FL, imagine wearing long sleeves and pant legs to cover scales.. UGH)
The Humira has done wonders for me.  I just wish they had it in pill form.

Previous meds have not helped with my crohns. Suffered for over 20 years. Numerous surgeries, fistulas, abcessess. After my 7th injection I started to notice significant improvements in my flare which had started in Feb 08 and did not let up until May 09. Mine are administered by homecare nurse, 2 shots, one each side of lower abdomen. And I got to avoid another surgery. Hope it continues to work!

I tried it for a year I have been on prednisone bursts most of the year with repeated flares. Don’t waist you time with this drug if you have moderate to sever RA.

This happened during my next two treatments, needless to say I'm no longer getting the infusions. It's a difficult situation because this is a very effective drug, yet it causes so many problems in the patient. Do your homework before choosing to start this treatment.

I was misdiagnosed with Ulcerative Colitis 12 years ago.  This year I was correctly diagnosed with Crohns.  I had my first Remicade IV treatment and 7 days later broke out with SEVERE HIVES.  I ended up in the ER and on steriods to control the hives.  No more Remicade for me that is for sure!

My 4yr. old daughter has been receiving remicade now for 10mo. for cronic uveitis. I was against this at first because of the potential side effects. So far so good. The medication seems to keep the inflamation down more so than the methotrexate did, and we have been able to ween her off of the several eyedrops she had been on for the last 1 1/2yrs. which caused a cataract. I am not sure how long she will be on Remicade but as far as I can see she is showing no worrysome side effects. She is as rambunctious, happy and healthy as any other 4yr old I have seen. Hope this helps out any other parents who might have a concern starting this medication.

I've taken Remicade infusion for over five years in response to anklyosing spondilitis (spinal fusion), and irritible bowel.  While Remicade hasn't helped my bowel condition a lot, it has been a miracle cure for alleviating all back pain I used to suffer.  Prior to treatment, my back pain was severe and affected my sleep.  Since going on treatment, I have never had any back pain whatsoever.  It really is a miracle drug for me and I highly recommend it.  I haven't had any negative reactions and the side effects are minimal for me - only a little fatigue.  The only downside to Remicade is its immunosuppresant nature.  You have to be careful with infections.  I work outdoors with the public all day long in the field of public safety and I've never had any complications or infections.

I have been on Opanna ER and Opana breakthru for 5 months. Find it to work well vs morphine or drugs like this. Some times 12 hours is to long between dosages. I am not a big fan of the breakthru.

I took Vyvanse for about 6 months and I have to say it was good and bad!It worked great (sometimes)!! But the side effects was awful!It made me very paranoid,like someone was always out to get me. I took Vyvance for almost 4 months. It help my mind to slow down and calm me down, I was also able to focus more.The down side was that it elavated my blood pressure and my Dr. had me stop taking it. I will try another medication in 3 weeks. He mentioned Stratara.

I was diagnosed iwth severe ADD a year and a half ago and started out on concerta (36mg x 2 / day). At the time I was on a PPO health plan which allowed me to get this med at $35 co-pay. Two months later I switched to an HSA with a $3,000 deductible. Having never checked the true price of the drug before I switched, I discovered that it's over $300 a month out of pocket. Not good... So, my doctor put me on Vyvanse which was half the cost, then Adderall. My results were mixed - Vyvanse was good but severely dehydrated me. My eyes, my mouth...I couldn't drink enough water during the day. Additionally, my sex drive evaporated. And when I did have sex, I was done in two minutes. NOT GOOD. I even had my testosterone levels checked and they were very good. Adderall had less side effects but wasn't as good as Vyvanse and still far less effective than Concerta. In the end, I went with concerta and for eight months I paid the $300+ a month out of pocket. Now, back on a PPO, I take Concerta and have actually increased my dosage as my body has "settled" into the medication. I now take three 32mg pills a day and it is working as it did when I started.  In the end, all I can say it that it's changed my life.  (FYI - I am 38, 6'5", 245)

Adding back one medication at a time, under doctors supervision, we discovered the Diovan was responsible. Switched to another medication which seems to work. I can fly again.

I was prescribed Diovan in hopes it would help lower by BP which can run 190/100. I've had high blood pressure for 23 yrs and have tried so many drugs it's not funny. Well, he didn't have to live with the side effects so I stopped taking it and guess what? No more diarrhea or feeling sick. Big Pharma should be sued for allowing some drugs to be on the market!

anyways, Nystatin seems be working for me. not no more pain just a slight cough and hoarse voice.

Prescribed at age 21 because the dose of I needed to derive any benefit out of Concerta also made me very sweaty and extremely anxious. While I still experience sweating - it's worse in the winter because it makes me so cold!! - clamminess and a little more edginess than I would without medication, it helped me have a great senior year of college. I also don't have as much difficulty sleeping as I did on Concerta.

I have been taking Concerta since December. I really didn't notice a difference until I got up to 72mg. I saw a huge change right away and an increase in my job performance. For the first time I had patience with my family! I even read a magazine for the first time (not just looking at the pictures). Recently though I feel it's not working as well. I have gone back to drinking TONS of caffeine even while taking the 72mg. I still feel like I could crash. I don't know if I am not getting enough sleep, need to take some time off, or need to try something new. I am starting to get "short" again and lose focus at work. Some days now I don't know if I even took it or not! All in all, it really made a positive impact on my life personally and professionally. I would recommend it. I think my personal situation warrants a change as my tolerance was built up very quickly. Other than that, only appetite loss (which for me was okay!).

I am a 54 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with inattentive type ADD. I began taking Concerta in addition to the Paxil and Klonopin which I had been on for about five years. I felt more focused, able to concentrate, and calmer within a few days. I started at 18 mg 3 weeks ago and now take 54 mg. With each dose increase I felt even more calm. I previously had high BP and a fast heart rate that I always believed was due to anxiety. Both my BP and heart rate have decreased since I started on Concerta. I am not jittery at all, have no stomach upset, no loss of appetite, and I actually sleep better, fall asleep faster and only wake up once during the night. I would have predicted that if I took a stimulant drug, I'd be bouncing off the walls! How wrong I was! I never would have thought it would calm me down, but that's what it does. My dr says it's a "paradoxical" reaction. My depression has improved--I now have hope that my life will get better now that I don't feel like I'm living in a fog all of the time. My memory has improved. Before, I couldn't remember simple instructions 30 seconds after they were give to me. I realized I had self-medicated with Sudafed and had been on the antidepressant Pamelor for a few years, but I had cardiac side effects and was taken off of it. I didn't realize that it was helping to treat my ADD symptoms at the time. I feel much better on Concerta--my only complaint is that I can feel it wear off 12 hours after I take it and I feel mad at the world at 5 PM! To counteract that my dr prescribed 10 mg Ritalin to help me from 5 PM to bedtime, so I can have some kind of life after work. I feel more motivated and have more physical energy than I've had in a long time.

For me the most disabling part of opiate withdrawal is (a.) crushing mental depression and (b.) a related lack of energy - when just getting up to go to the bathroom is a major chore. Clonidine just makes both of that worse. It's my *last choice* for opiate withdrawal. Ok, what clonidine will do is: alleviate restlesness & perhaps force you to rest if you're about to go crazy, but that's about all. I eventually found that having clonidine around *as a backup/adjunct to other w.d. aids* is more reliable. One example, kratom (a legal herbal opioid), totally reverses the mental depression & lack of energy - that's important when you've got a good job to keep. A Valium or two, here & there, maybe a clonidine if the blood pressure spikes. But as the sole agent in opioid withdrawal clonidine is a poor choice. The only drawback initially is that I had some difficulty locating words/names but this wore off. I've always been anti-medication but this drug has changed my mind-set!

topics.top_condition: Inability of Body to Handle Lactose or Milk Sugar
example_quotes: I lost both lobes of my thyroid to tumors - Hurthle Cell Carcinoma at the age of 40.  I am now 68.  For most of the interim, I took a strong dose of synthroid (generic did not work as well) to suppress any cancer cells that might have remained.  Recently two different doctors have advised me to reduce the synthroid to normal prescription levels and that has not caused any problems so far.   BUT I would like to share an odd story.   I am white, Anglo-Saxon and have always been able to eat cheeses and milk with no problem.  About 4 years ago, I became totally lactose intolerance and now I have to take Lactaid with any meal I suspect has milk products in it.   In researching how this could come about, I found that thyroid hormone in growing children is largely responsible for "maturing" their digestive systems so they don't digest mother's milk any more, which is totally normal in many races and most animals.  My humble opinion is that the continuous high doses of synthroid wiped out my ability to produce lactase enzyme and to digest milk products.  It has been surprising how many products in the U.S. contain milk, everything from popcorn to meatloaf, to salad dressings.

The worst thing is that they never mentioned ''vomiting'' as a side effect, but THEY SHOULD.
